item.title: Nonconformal kinetic theory with transverse dynamics and event-by-event simulations using CoMBolt-RTA
item.description:
Authors: Seyed Farid Taghavi

Updated: 2026-10-22

Category: nucl-th

Abstract:

A new version of CoMBolt, called CoMBolt-RTA, is introduced to solve the Boltzmann equation for massive quasiparticles in the relaxation time approximation (RTA). The inclusion of a constant quasiparticle mass allows one to obtain an equation of state (EOS) closer to that of lattice QCD. The nonequilibrium dynamics of a boost-invariant, nonconformal system with transverse spatial extension are studied, with particular emphasis on the effects of quasiparticle mass on the evolution toward equilibrium. Using the hybrid version, which includes TrENTo for the initial state and UrQMD as an afterburner, the model parameters are manually tuned to describe recent anisotropic-flow and charged-multiplicity measurements in OO collisions by the ALICE Collaboration. The resulting predictions for the $p_T$-spectrum and $\langle p_T\rangle$ are also compared with ATLAS measurements. Based on the preferred parameter tuning, the collective response as a function of opacity is investigated. The results suggest that central OO collisions remain in the fluid-like regime, while smaller systems, namely ${}^3$He-${}^3$He and ${}^4$He-${}^4$He collisions, could provide a better opportunity to investigate the transition from fluid-like to particle-like collective dynamics.

item.title: Charmed baryon-to-meson ratios inside jets as a discriminator of hadronization mechanisms: from color reconnection in p+p to coalescence in Pb+Pb
item.description:
Authors: Zi-Xuan Xu, Wei Dai, Ben-Wei Zhang, Enke Wang

Updated: 2026-10-22

Category: hep-ph

Abstract:

Jets separate the products of hard scatterings from the underlying event and thus help to clarify the origin of the enhanced baryon-to-meson ratios observed from small to large collision systems. We investigate the charmed baryon-to-meson ratio $Λ_c^+/D^0$ within jets in p+p and Pb+Pb collisions at $\sqrt{s_{NN}}=5.02$~TeV to discriminate between candidate hadronization mechanisms. In p+p collisions, simulated with PYTHIA8 using color reconnection (CR-BLC Mode 2) as a representative beyond-leading-color scenario, the in-jet ratio is enhanced at low-to-intermediate $p_T$ relative to the inclusive one---opposite to the light-flavor $Λ/K^0_S$ case---because the color-reconnection-induced excess of the ratio remains correlated with the jet and survives the jet requirement, while the fragmentation baseline shows no such enhancement. In Pb+Pb collisions, described by the SHELL model with a coalescence plus fragmentation hybrid hadronization, the in-jet ratio is instead suppressed moderately at intermediate $p_T$, because coalescence hadrons assembled from soft thermal partons carry no correlation with the jet direction and are preferentially discarded by the jet selection. The sign of the in-jet modification thus discriminates between the two mechanisms. Both mechanisms shift charmed hadrons toward small values of the parallel jet momentum fraction $z^{ch}_{||}$, with a stronger effect on $Λ_c^+$, so that the $z^{ch}_{||}$ spectrum probes non-fragmentation hadronization independently of parton energy loss. The radial profile of the in-jet ratio rises with the distance from the jet axis in both systems, with the lowest-$p_T$ interval displaced farthest for color reconnection and the intermediate-$p_T$ interval for coalescence. These results provide the baseline and predictions needed for future jet-tagged charmed-hadron measurements in both collision systems.

item.title: Heavy-Quark Dynamics from $D^{0}$-Meson Anisotropy-Response Scaling Violations
item.description:
Authors: Roy A. Lacey

Updated: 2026-10-21

Category: nucl-ex

Abstract:

A species-resolved anisotropy-response scaling framework is used to investigate heavy-quark dynamics through the elliptic ($v_2$) and triangular ($v_3$) azimuthal anisotropies of $D^0$ mesons. The independently constrained light-flavor response provides a direct null test: the transformed $D^0$ harmonics exhibit approximate inter-harmonic closure but remain systematically displaced from the kaon-anchored scaling function, revealing a charm scaling violation. The common response is recovered through a charm-specific attenuation rescaling, $k_c$, together with a small low-$p_T$ hadronic-rescattering correction, $ζ_{\rm hs}\simeq0.06$, while retaining the established light-flavor prescription. In Pb+Pb collisions at $\sqrt{s_{NN}}=5.02$~TeV, $k_c$ decreases from approximately $2.0$ in central and mid-central collisions to $1.27$ in the 30--50\% interval. For $D^0$ $v_2$, ultra-central p+Pb collisions at $\sqrt{s_{NN}}=8.16$~TeV require $k_c\simeq1.5$, whereas Au+Au collisions at $\sqrt{s_{NN}}=200$~GeV are consistent with $k_c\simeq1$. The transition momentum exhibits a distinct system dependence: $D^0$ and light mesons show comparable $p_{T,\rm tr}\simeq4.5$--$5.0$~GeV/$c$ in Pb+Pb, consistent with the common large-system prescription also used in Au+Au, whereas p+Pb $D^0$ measurements are consistent with the lower light-meson scale of approximately $1.6$~GeV/$c$. These complementary constraints on attenuation strength and transition momentum provide a differential benchmark for heavy-quark transport and medium evolution.

item.title: Generalized Coordinate Bethe Ansatz and Quantum Integrability of the Time-Dependent Massive Thirring Model
item.description:
Authors: Parameshwar R. Pasnoori

Updated: 2026-10-21

Category: math-ph

Abstract:

We develop a generalized coordinate Bethe-ansatz framework for the massive Thirring model with an explicitly time-dependent fermion mass. Unlike the generalized Bethe ansatz for chiral quantum field theories, where particle transport acts in internal spin spaces and leads to quantum Knizhnik-Zamolodchikov equations, the present construction acts directly on particle coordinates and physical rapidities. Its central new feature is a rapidity lattice. Because the time-dependent mass couples right- and left-moving components already in the one-particle sector, a fixed-rapidity block is not closed under spatial winding. Periodicity therefore requires all sectors generated by the finite shift $β\toβ-p$. Particle exchange relates amplitudes on this lattice through scalar analytic difference equations of Ruijsenaars type, whose solutions determine the complete time-dependent many-body wavefunction. Consistency of the coordinate construction also selects an exponential evolution of the bare mass, providing a new realization of the time dependent integrability-renormalization group correspondence. In the static limit, the rapidity-lattice construction reduces to the conventional massive-Thirring Bethe equations. Through the massive-Thirring/sine Gordon equivalence, the result also connects this exact quantum construction to the generalized space-time dependent Lax formalism.

item.title: Nuclear Geometry-Driven Femtoscopic Correlations in Light-Ion Collisions
item.description:
Authors: Dániel Kincses, Bithika Karmakar, Iurii Karpenko, Boris Tomášik

Updated: 2026-10-21

Category: nucl-th

Abstract:

Recent anisotropic flow measurements in $^{16}\rm O{+}^{16}\rm O$ and $^{20}\rm Ne{+}^{20}\rm Ne$ collisions at a center-of-mass energy per nucleon pair of 5.36~TeV provide evidence for nuclear geometry-driven collectivity. In this Letter, we investigate the femtoscopic signatures of nuclear geometry in these light-ion collision systems, using a hybrid simulation framework that couples \textit{ab initio} nuclear configurations to viscous hydrodynamics and hadronic transport. We show that the $\rm Ne{+}Ne/O{+}O$ ratio of the freeze-out eccentricity, extracted from azimuthally sensitive femtoscopy, reaches 1.5-1.8 in central collisions for deformed nuclear configurations, compared with about unity for a spherical baseline. This enhancement is significantly larger than that of elliptic flow in the same simulations, and remains stable when pre-equilibrium free streaming is omitted, even though the absolute source radii change considerably. Confronting these predictions with future data will provide new, complementary constraints on nuclear structure and initial-condition modeling.

item.title: UrQMD-Agent: An LLM-Assisted Framework for Microscopic Tracing of Proton Azimuthal Correlations
item.description:
Authors: Fu-Peng Li, Yige Huang

Updated: 2026-10-21

Category: nucl-th

Abstract:

We present an LLM-assisted framework for microscopic transport studies that connects a general-purpose large language model (LLM) to the UrQMD transport model through a model-specific Skill and a deterministic scientific tool layer. The LLM supports literature-guided scientific planning and interpretation, while numerical calculations, event-history reconstruction, and statistical analyses are performed by deterministic tools. As a demonstration, the framework is applied to proton azimuthal-partition fluctuations in Au+Au collisions at $\sqrt{s_{NN}}=3.0$--39~GeV. In the 0--5\% centrality class, the fluctuations are statistically resolved below zero from 3 to 27~GeV and consistent with zero at 39~GeV. An exact pair-kernel decomposition shows that the negative signal is carried mainly by proton pairs containing at least one decay-fed proton. A random-label null test further distinguishes the observed pair contributions from expectations based on pair abundance alone. Reaction-history tracing shows that, for pairs of two decay-fed protons, the negative pair-kernel contribution is already present in the parent momenta evaluated at their respective formation vertices. The modular architecture is designed to accommodate different general-purpose LLMs and can be extended to other microscopic transport models through dedicated Skills and tool interfaces. This provides a pathway toward systematic microscopic analyses and comparisons across transport models within a common LLM-assisted framework.

item.title: Digital Quantum Simulation of Dynamics in Interacting Fields
item.description:
Authors: Zhiyao Li

Updated: 2026-10-20

Category: quant-ph

Abstract:

Matter under extreme conditions behaves as a non-equilibrium, strongly-interacting quantum system. Such systems are in the non-perturbative regime of quantum chromodynamics (QCD), where their time evolution is classically intractable. Quantum computing offers a promising alternative, but present-day devices are limited in qubit count and circuit depth, so efficient formulations and algorithms are key to scaling toward experimentally relevant QCD simulations. A scalable framework is established for simulating energy loss and hadronization in 1+1-dimensional SU(2) lattice gauge theory, in which a heavy quark traverses a lattice of light quarks. Classical lattice QCD methods are translated into physics-informed circuits to prepare the interacting ground state. The evolution is run on IBM's quantum processor ibm_pittsburgh, where the charge distribution and energy loss are measured. A further study develops the quantum simulation of the fully gauge-fixed SU(2) Hamiltonian in a mixed basis, a formulation that is expected to remain efficient at all gauge couplings. Digitizing the continuous gauge fields with as few as three qubits per plaquette reproduces low-energy observables with $10^{-3}$ precision. Scaling to larger systems is limited by resource overhead, which motivates truncations that preserve the relevant observables. Sequency Hierarchy Truncation (SeqHT) exploits the hierarchy in basis-operator contributions. Demonstrated on the adiabatic preparation of the $λφ^4$ ground state on ibm_sherbrooke, SeqHT reduces circuit depth by ~30%, suppressing hardware noise in the extracted observables. All simulations in this dissertation are validated on quantum hardware against classical benchmarks. These studies advance quantum simulations of real-time QCD dynamics.

item.title: Heavy-quark thermalization in the quark-gluon plasma via a fractional Langevin equation
item.description:
Authors: Jai Prakash, Mohammad Yousuf Jamal, Shanshan Cao, Guang-You Qin, Yifeng Sun

Updated: 2026-10-20

Category: nucl-th

Abstract:

The dynamics of heavy quarks in the quark-gluon plasma is commonly described within a standard Langevin equation framework. In this work, we extend the conventional framework by using a fractional Langevin equation based on the Caputo derivative of order $α$ with $1<α\leq 2$. We solve the fractional Langevin equation and derive the corresponding {\textit {fractional fluctuation-dissipation theorem}} for the heavy quark thermalization in the quark-gluon plasma medium. We calculate the time evolution of the mean-squared momentum, mean-squared displacement, momentum distribution, energy loss, longitudinal momentum loss, transverse momentum broadening, and the nuclear suppression factor of the heavy quarks. The mean-squared momentum thermalizes to the same value for all $α$ at late times, in agreement with the fractional fluctuation-dissipation theorem, and the nuclear suppression factor shows a systematic $α$-dependence. The energy loss of an energetic heavy quark grows strongly with $α$. The time evolution of the heavy quark momentum distribution provides additional sensitivity to the fractional dynamics of the heavy quarks in the QGP medium.

item.title: Measurements of local polarization of $Λ$ hyperons with event shape engineering in Au+Au collisions at RHIC-STAR
item.description:
Authors: Taiki Kondo

Updated: 2026-10-20

Category: nucl-ex

Abstract:

Anisotropic flow is expected to generate local vorticities along the beam direction, which in turn lead to local polarization of produced particles. Although the local polarization of hyperons has already been observed at RHIC and the LHC, its mechanism is not yet understood: model calculations indicate that the shear-induced and vorticity-induced contributions can have opposite signs and may substantially cancel, so that the resulting polarization depends sensitively on the theoretical implementation. Since both are driven by the anisotropic flow, we employ the Event Shape Engineering (ESE) method, which selects events with different flow magnitudes within a narrow centrality range, to measure the local polarization as a function of the elliptic flow at a fixed multiplicity. We report the measurements of the elliptic flow ($v_2$) and the local polarization ($P_{z,2}$) of $Λ$ and $\barΛ$ as a function of the reduced flow vector magnitude $q_2$ used for the ESE event selection, in Au+Au collisions at $\sqrt{s_{\rm NN}} = 19.6~{\rm GeV}$ from the STAR experiment. The $v_2$ shows a clear positive dependence on $q_2$, while $P_{z,2}$ indicates a weak positive dependence on $q_2$ and $v_2$. This is the first measurement to directly investigate the relation between anisotropic flow and local polarization, providing new insight into the origin of local polarization.

item.title: Jets as differential probes of hot QCD matter
item.description:
Authors: João M. Silva

Updated: 2026-10-19

Category: hep-ph

Abstract:

Ultra-relativistic heavy-ion collisions create short-lived droplets of deconfined, hot QCD matter whose evolution connects far-from-equilibrium early dynamics to the hydrodynamic quark-gluon plasma. High-energy jets, produced in early hard scatterings and modified by this evolving medium, provide multi-scale probes of its microscopic properties. This thesis develops perturbative QCD tools to extract information about hot QCD matter from its imprint on differential jet substructure observables. Our framework is the BDMPS-Z description of high-energy partons propagating through stochastic colour fields. We first study anisotropic QCD matter by replacing the usual scalar broadening parameter with direction-dependent transverse momentum broadening. This relates anisotropic corrections to medium-induced splittings to spin information and azimuthal patterns in final-state energy flow. Energy correlators are then used as observables sensitive to these effects, including heavy-flavour EECs, azimuthally differential EECs and clover projections designed to isolate leading anisotropy-induced harmonics. We also examine how energy loss affects the interpretation of jet substructure modifications. Quantile matching defines reconstructed energy loss as a population-level shift between vacuum and medium-modified jet spectra. We further develop energy-loss functions, which encode the distribution of energy retained by jet-originated hadrons, and show how their moments enter multi-point projected energy correlators. Finally, we go beyond single $1\to2$ medium-induced splittings by studying spin-induced correlations between successive emissions and higher-point energy correlators including contributions from medium response. The results show that differential jet substructure can probe directional properties of QCD matter and multi-point dynamics of jets propagating through it.

item.title: Fluctuations of $v_2$ versus fluctuations of $\varepsilon_2$: Beyond linear and cubic response
item.description:
Authors: Andreas Kirchner, Mubarak Alqahtani, Jean-Yves Ollitrault

Updated: 2026-10-19

Category: nucl-th

Abstract:

Elliptic flow ($v_2$) is the most prominent signature of collective flow in heavy-ion collisions. Its event-by-event fluctuations are accurately measured in Pb+Pb collisions at the LHC. They originate from the early stages of the collision, and are usually understood in terms of linear response to the initial anisotropy $\varepsilon_2$, with a small cubic correction. We reveal deviations from this scenario on the basis of extensive event-by-event hydrodynamic simulations. We analyze the hydrodynamic response order by order in the cumulant expansion of $\varepsilon_2$ and $v_2$ fluctuations. We carry out this expansion in the "intrinsic frame" where the magnitude and direction of the impact parameter are fixed. We find that the asymmetry of $v_2$ fluctuations is opposite to that of $\varepsilon_2$ fluctuations. We also find that the response to $\varepsilon_2$ fluctuations is larger by $\approx 10-20\%$ than the response to the average geometry. This effect, which is not explained by the cubic response, increases the splitting between $v_2\{2\}$ and $v_2\{4\}$.

item.title: Transverse momentum dependent parton distributions at small $x$
item.description:
Authors: Paul Caucal, Farid Salazar

Updated: 2026-10-19

Category: hep-ph

Abstract:

Transverse-momentum-dependent (TMD) parton distributions provide a three-dimensional description of the momentum structure of hadrons. They are probed in proton-proton and proton-nucleus collisions at the LHC and RHIC, and are a central part of the physics program of the future Electron-Ion Collider (EIC). While TMD factorization is well established at moderate Bjorken $x$, the small-$x$ regime requires a different treatment, since large logarithms of $1/x$ must be resummed and non-linear effects due to high gluon densities become important. The Color Glass Condensate (CGC) effective theory provides a natural framework to describe TMDs in this saturation regime and to connect them with standard TMD factorization. This chapter reviews quark and gluon TMDs at small $x$, covering operator definitions, gauge-link structures, and Wilson-line correlators in the CGC for unpolarized and polarized distributions. We discuss factorization for inclusive and diffractive observables, highlighting the role of process dependence and the emergence of a limited set of Wilson-line operators. We then summarize the evolution of these distributions, namely the resummation of logarithms of $1/x$ by the Balitsky-Kovchegov and JIMWLK equations, and of Sudakov logarithms of the hard scale through Collins-Soper-Sterman evolution. We also review TMDs beyond the eikonal approximation, including the sub-eikonal Wilson-line operators that give access to helicity and other spin-dependent distributions, their double-logarithmic small-$x$ evolution and the resulting asymptotics, and the sub-eikonal corrections to the eikonal distributions, which provide a first step toward the moderate-$x$ regime. Finally, we discuss phenomenological implications for present and future experiments, with emphasis on the EIC, and outline the theoretical challenges toward a unified description of TMDs.

item.title: Parton Fragmentation Functions
item.description:
Authors: Hongxi Xing

Updated: 2026-10-19

Category: hep-ph

Abstract:

This chapter provides a pedagogical and comprehensive introduction to parton fragmentation functions (FFs), the essential non-perturbative quantities in Quantum Chromodynamics (QCD) that describe the universal process of hadronization, the transition of quarks and gluons into observable hadrons. Formally defined as gauge-invariant matrix elements, the determination of FFs is achieved through global QCD analyses that synthesize world data from three primary processes: electron-positron annihilation, semi-inclusive deep inelastic scattering, and proton-proton collisions. This chapter covers the theoretical foundations of FFs, including their operator definitions and properties, the experimental probes used to constrain them, and the methodologies of modern global analyses. The discussion is extended to more advanced topics, including dihadron FFs, the three-dimensional picture of hadronization provided by spin- and transverse-momentum-dependent FFs, and the modification of fragmentation in a nuclear medium, which is key to probe their fundamental properties.

item.title: Linear Structure, Convergence and Resurgence of Hydrodynamic Transseries
item.description:
Authors: Qi Zhou, Enke Wang, Hui Zhang

Updated: 2026-10-18

Category: nucl-th

Abstract:

We construct an exact formulation for the solution of Bjorken expanding relativistic viscous hydrodynamics with a constant relaxation time and derive its late time transseries structure. The two fundamental modes of the linear auxiliary equation separate the hydrodynamic contribution from the exponentially suppressed transient mode. We show that this single transient mode generates the entire hierarchy of nonperturbative sectors through nonlinear mode mixing, while its decay explains the loss of initial condition dependence and the emergence of late time hydrodynamic attractor behavior. The hydrodynamic gradient expansion is factorially divergent for generic values of the transport parameter but converges at the discrete values $a=N^2$, where the auxiliary asymptotic expansions terminate. We further determine the exact Stokes constant of the auxiliary linear equation and establish its relation to the logarithmic Borel singularity coefficient. The vanishing of the Stokes constant at these exceptional values establishes a direct connection between auxiliary series termination, hydrodynamic convergence, and Stokes decoupling between the hydrodynamic and the nonhydrodynamic transient sector.

item.title: BeAGLE++: A modern modular framework for eA physics at the EIC
item.description:
Authors: Arjun Kumar, Abhay Deshpande, Zhoudunming Tu

Updated: 2026-10-16

Category: hep-ph

Abstract:

We present the Benchmark eA Generator for LEptoproduction (BeAGLE++), a next-generation, general-purpose Monte Carlo event generator for high-energy lepton-nucleus collisions and the successor to BeAGLE. The framework incorporates a formation-zone intranuclear cascade to describe hadronic final-state interactions (FSIs), followed by statistical de-excitation of the residual nucleus. Compared with the legacy implementation, the BeAGLE++ cascade introduces a discrete time-ordered treatment of hadronic interactions and light-cluster production during intranuclear transport. Comparisons with E665 measurements and legacy BeAGLE calculations show broad agreement for selected observables, while revealing differences in final states sensitive to FSIs. These differences provide opportunities to assess the model dependence of nuclear-breakup predictions and constrain the underlying cascade dynamics. With its modular architecture, BeAGLE++ provides a flexible simulation framework for the Electron-Ion Collider (EIC) and a platform for developing and testing new physics models against existing data and future EIC measurements.

item.title: Proton-Number Fluctuations in $^{238}$U+$^{238}$U Collisions at $\sqrt{s_{\mathrm{NN}}} = 2.1$ GeV with the CEE Fast Simulation
item.description:
Authors: Shuaike Lv, Fan Si, Xionghong He, Xu Sun, Yige Huang, Wanbing He, Yifei Zhang, Ming Shao, Ziyang Li

Updated: 2026-10-16

Category: nucl-ex

Abstract:

The Cooling Storage Ring External-target Experiment (CEE) at the Heavy Ion Research Facility in Lanzhou (HIRFL) offers a unique opportunity to map the QCD phase diagram in the high-baryon-density region. In particular, higher-order cumulants ($C_r$) of event-by-event proton number distributions have been proposed as sensitive probes of the nuclear-matter phase structure. In this work, $^{\text{238}}$U+$^{\text{238}}$U collisions at $\sqrt{s_{\mathrm{NN}}} = 2.1$ GeV are generated using the JAM2 model and then processed through the CEE fast simulation with detector responses. Experimental analysis procedures, including centrality determination and particle identification, are also implemented. Proton-number cumulants up to fourth order and their ratios are calculated and compared with the true values. A track-by-track efficiency correction method is tested by introducing reconstruction efficiency within the TPC acceptance. An additional factor is also included to account for acceptance losses caused by the azimuthal gap between the two TPCs. Within the uncertainties of the current data sample, the corrected cumulants and cumulant ratios are consistent with their generator-level values. The event-sample dependence of the cumulant-ratio uncertainties is further investigated to estimate the statistics required for future measurements, revealing a substantial statistical cost associated with the acceptance compensation. These results provide a simulation-based assessment of the analysis feasibility and statistical requirements for proton-number fluctuation measurements at CEE.

item.title: Anisotropic hadronic matter in external magnetic fields
item.description:
Authors: Dushmanta Sahu, Jayanta Dey

Updated: 2026-10-16

Category: hep-ph

Abstract:

Strong magnetic fields generated in non-central heavy-ion collisions break rotational symmetry and can imprint anisotropy on the produced quantum chromodynamics (QCD) matter. Within a hadron resonance gas framework in the presence of an external magnetic field, we investigate the resulting anisotropy in the equation of state, isothermal compressibility, speed of sound, and conserved-charge fluctuations. We find that the electric-charge susceptibility ratio $χ_4^Q/χ_2^Q$ develops a pronounced directional dependence, driven primarily by the Landau-level structure of charged pions. For physically relevant magnetic fields, this anisotropy reaches $\sim 10 - 15 \%$ at $T\simeq0.16$ GeV. The ratio of electric-charge susceptibility can be expressed as $χ_4^Q/χ_2^Q=C_4^Q/C_2^Q=κ_Qσ_Q^2$, where $C_2^Q$ and $C_4^Q$ are the second- and fourth-order cumulants, and $κ_Q$ and $σ_Q$ are the kurtosis and variance of the event-by-event net-electric-charge distribution. The reaction-plane dependence of this ratio provides an experimentally accessible signature of magnetic-field-induced anisotropy. Our results identify higher-order electric-charge fluctuations as a promising probe of the imprint of strong electromagnetic fields on the matter produced in heavy-ion collisions at RHIC and the LHC.

item.title: Exploring QCD Matter through Energy Correlators of Soft Hadrons
item.description:
Authors: Yiyang Peng, João Barata, Andrey V. Sadofyev, Huichao Song

Updated: 2026-10-15

Category: nucl-th

Abstract:

We propose energy-energy correlators (EECs) of soft hadrons and their azimuthal harmonics as new soft observables to probe the collective flow and correlations beyond flow for large and small systems created in high energy nuclear collisions. We separate the soft EEC into a disconnected contribution determined by the mean energy flow and a connected contribution encoding correlations beyond it. Viscous hydrodynamic simulations demonstrate that the soft EEC of a fluid system is governed by the disconnected contribution, while its elliptic and triangular harmonics respond to the initial geometry and shear viscosity as traditional flow harmonics do. Comparisons between iEBE-VISHNU and PYTHIA for p+p, O+O, and Pb+Pb collisions show that the disconnected contribution dominates at large angles in all systems, whereas connected correlations beyond the mean energy flow grow toward small angles and small systems, most strongly for the harmonics. Soft EECs thus provide a unique window into collective flow and correlations beyond it across collision systems.

item.title: Experimental review on global polarization and spin alignment in heavy-ion collisions
item.description:
Authors: Takafumi Niida

Updated: 2026-10-15

Category: nucl-ex

Abstract:

Polarization phenomena in heavy-ion collisions have attracted considerable interest since the first experimental observation of global spin polarization. Over the past few years, particle polarization has emerged as a rapidly growing field, with new measurements that have stimulated intense theoretical efforts to understand the puzzling experimental results. In these proceedings, we review recent experimental progress on hyperon global polarization, local polarization along the beam direction, and vector-meson spin alignment in relativistic heavy-ion collisions, and newly emerging measurements of spin-spin correlations. These measurements provide new insights into the vortical structure of the quark-gluon plasma and the spin dynamics during the system evolution.

item.title: Nuclear PDFs
item.description:
Authors: K. Greve, T. Ježo, M. Klasen, A. Kusina, F. I. Olness, J. Wissmann

Updated: 2026-10-15

Category: hep-ph

Abstract:

We summarize the current status of global analyses of model-independent nuclear parton distri- bution functions (nPDFs). A carefully conducted global analysis of nPDFs in the era of heavy-ion collisions at the LHC is key to gaining access to new information through the data measured by the collider experiments. This implies incorporating as large and diverse a dataset as possible, as well as the latest theoretical calculations, in order to capture a faithful representation of nuclear structure that reflects the current state of knowledge. On the other hand, the uncertainties in par- ticular must reflect what is not known. For many observables, nuclear uncertainties represent the most significant source of error in current theoretical models; nevertheless, they should not, where possible, be artificially constrained (for example, through parameterization bias). The quality of a global (n)PDF fit is often measured by the $χ^2$ per degree of freedom, which is approximately one for a fit that describes the data precisely without overfitting. Many additional aspects allow to characterize a good fit, e.g. the $χ^2$ distribution per experiment, the shape of the uncertainties, and the sensitivity to different types of data. We inspect various fit quality indicators for fits obtained by different groups. Morever we pay close attention to the $A$-dependence. Traditionally, the A-dependence had a primarily functional role in global nPDF analyses and comparatively less attention has been paid to it when characterizing a fit. However, we have now entered the era of nuclei collisions at the LHC and need to investigate the $A$-dependence properly.

item.title: No Einstein Relation, No Problem: How Relativistic Weakly Coupled Heavy Quarks Equilibrate Beyond Leading Logarithm Anyway
item.description:
Authors: Jean F. Du Plessis, Bruno Scheihing-Hitschfeld

Abstract:

item.title: How Quantum Is Bottomonium in the Quark-Gluon Plasma?
item.description:
Authors: Nora Brambilla, Tom Magorsch

Updated: 2026-10-01

Abstract:

We further show that the position-space coherence is similarly suppressed and plateaus close to the 1S value. We trace the finite residual quantum structure to conditional purification: the medium preferentially dissolves weakly bound and unbound modes with large $\langle r^2\rangle$, driving the surviving singlet $\mathrm{S}$-wave ensemble toward the $1\mathrm{S}$ state. Additionally, the spatial dependence of the chiral crossover transition is examined through the radial variation of the pseudocritical temperature. We find that the pseudocritical temperature decreases with increasing radial distance, indicating that the chiral crossover sets in at progressively lower temperatures as one goes away from the rotation axis.

item.title: Photon-induced $J/ψ$ as a linearly polarized probe of collision geometry in relativistic heavy-ion collisions
item.description:
Authors: STAR Collaboration

Updated: 2026-09-13

Category: nucl-ex

Abstract:

In relativistic heavy-ion collisions, the linear polarization of quasi-real photons can correlate the spin orientation of photon-induced vector mesons with the collision geometry. To explore this sensitivity, we present the first measurement of the decay angular distribution of photon-induced $J/ψ$ with respect to the event plane in heavy-ion collisions with hadronic overlap. The analysis uses Ru+Ru and Zr+Zr collisions at a nucleon--nucleon center-of-mass energy of $\sqrt{s_{\mathrm{NN}}}=200$ GeV recorded by STAR. After correcting for the finite event-plane resolution and subtracting the residual hadronic contribution, we extract a negative second-order modulation, $A_2^{\rm phot} = -0.39 \pm 0.11~(\mathrm{stat.}) \pm 0.04~(\mathrm{sys.})$, for $|y^{ee}|<0.8$, $p_{\mathrm T}^{ee}<0.2~\mathrm{GeV}/c$, and 30--80% centrality. This modulation provides evidence that the $J/ψ$ polarization is correlated with the event plane, as expected for linearly polarized photons. The observed modulation establishes polarized $J/ψ$ photoproduction as a direct probe of the transverse orientation of the initial collision geometry.

item.title: Collinear fragmentation of pseudoscalar quarkonia from NLO NRQCD
item.description:
Authors: Francesco Giovanni Celiberto, Francesca Lonigro

Updated: 2026-09-10

Category: hep-ph

Abstract:

We discuss a new family of publicly available collinear fragmentation functions (FFs) for pseudoscalar quarkonia, the NRFF1.0 set. It builds upon the Heavy-Flavor Non-Relativistic evolution (HF-NRevo) scheme, designed to describe heavy-hadron formation through leading-power fragmentation at moderate and large transverse momentum. Heavy-quarkonium production naturally involves both perturbative and non-perturbative QCD dynamics, from the production of the heavy $Q\bar{Q}$ pair to its formation into a physical bound state. Within NRFF1.0, Non-Relativistic Quantum Chromodynamics (NRQCD) provides the theoretical framework for calculating the FF inputs at the initial scale, which are subsequently evolved through the HF-NRevo scheme. This setup provides a precision baseline for investigating the underlying partonic hierarchy and jet structure across the moderate- to high-transverse-momentum regime. The explicit treatment of partonic channels and heavy-flavor thresholds makes this framework particularly suitable for exploring quarkonium-in-jet fragmentation, jet-quenching sensitivity, energy-loss mechanisms, and the emergence of medium-modified fragmentation patterns in the quark-gluon plasma.

item.title: Study of the multiplicity dependence of non-flow correlations in pp collisions at $\sqrt{s}=200$ GeV using PYTHIA
item.description:
Authors: Milan Stojanovic, Joern Putschke

Updated: 2026-09-10

Category: nucl-th

Abstract:

The observation of a near-side enhancement in long-range correlations within high-multiplicity pA and pp collisions, commonly referred to as the ridge, has motivated significant efforts to quantify possible collective effects in small systems. Estimation of non-flow contributions in two-particle correlation measurements in small systems at the LHC typically relies on the assumption that jet-induced non-flow correlations are independent of event multiplicity. Consequently, this assumption allows the high-multiplicity non-flow to be estimated and accounted for by directly using low-multiplicity events. In this paper, the validity of this assumption is studied examining the multiplicity dependence of non-flow contributions estimated via two-particle correlation functions in pp collisions at RHIC energies $\sqrt{s} = 200$~GeV using the PYTHIA event generator. It is observed that selecting any specific multiplicity range inherently biases jet production dynamics. These biases introduce a non-trivial multiplicity dependence of the non-flow contribution at RHIC energies. The dependence of jet fragmentation and $p_{\text{T}}$-differential cross sections on event multiplicity is studied using a variety of commonly used multiplicity estimators, including mid-rapidity charged-particle multiplicity, forward multiplicity, and underlying-event activity. The results indicate that non-flow contributions do not exhibit simple multiplicity scaling and challenge the applicability of standard subtraction procedures utilized at LHC energies at lower RHIC collision energies.

item.title: Qubit-Qutrit Quantum Tomography of hadronic $Λφ$ and $ΛK^{\ast 0}$ systems
item.description:
Authors: Veronica Kanachova, Feng Liu, Zhoudunming Tu

Updated: 2026-09-10

Category: hep-ph

Abstract:

Quantum-information observables have emerged in recent years as new tools in nuclear and particle physics, from entanglement in top-quark pairs to spin correlations in $Λ\barΛ$ production. Extending these studies to unequal-spin hadronic final states poses a fundamental challenge: the $6\times6$ density matrix of a qubit-qutrit system contains 35 independent spin parameters, but the decays of $ΛV$ pairs, with $V=φ$ or $K^{*0}$, provide access to only 23 due to the hidden vector polarization from the strong decay. In this Letter, we formulate a qubit-qutrit quantum tomography (QQQT) technique for these spin-$\tfrac{1}{2}\otimes1$ systems and establish exact criteria for entanglement certification from the \textit{incomplete} density matrix. Compared with the $Λ\barΛ$ system, QQQT of $Λφ$ and $ΛK^{*0}$ provides a new probe of nonperturbative QCD hadronization, enabling a direct comparison of the spin evolution of entangled quark pairs produced from the vacuum as they hadronize into a baryon or a vector meson.

item.title: Production of Light Nuclei and Hypernuclei in Heavy-Ion Collisions
item.description:
Authors: Guannan Xie, Yue-Hang Leung

Updated: 2026-09-10

Category: hep-ex

Abstract:

We review recent STAR and ALICE measurements of light-nucleus and hypernucleus yields, femtoscopic correlations, and collective flow presented at SQM 2026. Statistical-hadronization calculations provide a useful baseline for integrated yields but do not simultaneously describe all measured light-nucleus ratios across collision energies and system sizes. For bound states with mass number $A<4$, current coalescence calculations provide a broadly consistent description of yields, femtoscopic correlations, and collective flow, although the quantitative hypertriton comparison depends on the assumed few-body wave function. The suppressed production of resonant $^{4}$Li relative to compact $^{4}$He indicates an effect of nuclear structure and late-stage dynamics. However, the quantitative model comparison also depends on the treatment of feed-down from unstable states. In high-multiplicity $p$+$p$ collisions, pion-deuteron femtoscopy further indicates that most observed (anti)deuterons are formed through nucleon fusion after strong decays of short-lived resonances. Taken together, these measurements show that production chronology and internal nuclear structure leave measurable imprints on the physics observables.

item.title: A detailed view at magnetic dipole strengths: The case of semi-magic $^{50}$Ti
item.description:
Authors: B. Kelly, M. Spieker, U. Friman-Gayer, L. T. Baby, T. Beck, A. L. Conley, S. W. Finch, J. Isaak, Krishichayan, E. Litvinova, H. Pai, N. Pietralla, D. Savran, W. Tornow, N. Tsoneva, A. Volya, V. Werner

Updated: 2026-09-09

Category: nucl-ex

Abstract:

Magnetic dipole, $M1$, strengths were studied in semi-magic $^{50}$Ti up to the neutron-separation threshold by combining data from $(d,p)$ one-neutron transfer, $(γ,γ')$ real-photon scattering, $(e,e')$ inelastic scattering at extreme backward angles, and $(p,p')$ at $E_p = 210$ MeV and extreme forward angles. The combination of all probes provided unique access to the neutron spin-flip contribution and the possibility to evaluate its role in generating the spin-flip $M1$ strengths. The small contribution of the neutron $(1f_{7/2})^{-1}(1f_{5/2})^{+1}$ spin-flip transitions, which were probed with the $(d,p)$ reaction, to the overall strength in $^{50}$Ti questions the standard picture for the microscopic origin of spin-flip strength in the $fp$ shell. For $^{50}$Ti, this letter shows that $J^π = 1^+$ states with larger neutron $(1f_{7/2})^{-1}(1f_{5/2})^{+1}$ spectroscopic factors do not correspond to the ones with the largest $B(M1;0^+_1 \rightarrow 1^+_i)$ strengths.
